SparkR / SPARKR-148
Error in .jfindClass(o) : class not found
Issue Type: Bug
Assignee: Unassigned
Created: 23/Dec/14 8:32 PM
Environment:

Windows 8, 64-bit
Priority: Major
Reporter: Simon Ouellette

I installed SparkR in R 64-bit version 3.1.2 using the install_github line.

It completed with a success message, and I am able to load SparkR by doing library(SparkR). It responds with:

Loading required package: rJava
[SparkR] Initializing with classpath C:/Program\ Files/R/R-3.1.2/library/SparkR/sparkr-assembly-0.1.jar

But then when I do:
> sc <- sparkR.init(master="local")

I get the error message:
Error in .jfindClass(o) : class not found

I have verified that the above .jar exists and is indeed at the expected location.

Note that I am using Java SDK/JRE 1.8 (64-bit). I am running Spark 1.2.0 on Hadoop 2.3. All in Windows 8, 64-bit.

Hmm – Do you have a more complete stack trace ? Usually it should print something which says which class was not found etc.
Usually this error message means that something didn't get built properly (i.e. the assembly jar is missing some class)

Re: Error in .jfindClass(o) : class not found

Thanks for the stack trace. The problem seems to be that in both cases we are not able to find the class RRDD inside the JAR (Just to confirm, the stack trace looks similar for the binary build as well ?). I am not very sure why this is happening, but there are a couple of things we could try

1. I've previously seen some problems with install locations having spaces (like 'Program\ Files'). Is there any chance you could try installing SparkR in a location without spaces ?
2. You can also inspect the contents of the JAR file and see if the RRDD class is present. I am not sure how to do this in Windows, but in linux you can use the `jar -tvf <jar_file_name>` to list all the files in the JAR. Actually I just did this for the binary build and it does have all the classes.
